accepted.question_text: Let f(n) denote the number of partitions of the integer n for which every nonzero multiplicity of a part is distinct. The paper proves the first-order asymptotic behavior of ln f(n). What are the lower-order terms in the asymptotic expansion of ln f(n)?
accepted.context_brief: Lower-order asymptotics of log-count of Wilf partitions

evidence.quote: We have found the first-order asymptotic description of ln f(n), but lower-order terms of ln f(n) remain unknown.

accepted.question_text: Let f(n) denote the number of partitions of the integer n for which every nonzero multiplicity of a part is distinct. Determine the first-order asymptotic behavior of f(n) itself, not just of ln f(n).
accepted.context_brief: First-order asymptotics of Wilf partition counts

evidence.quote: A Herculean task would be to find the first-order asymptotic description of f(n) itself.

accepted.question_text: Let f(n) denote the number of partitions of the integer n for which every nonzero multiplicity of a part is distinct. Is f(n) a nondecreasing function of n; that is, does f(n + 1) >= f(n) for all positive integers n?

evidence.quote: As a much simpler task, David S. Newman has mentioned that it would be nice to have a proof that f(n) is nondecreasing.

accepted.question_text: Let T(n) be the set of partitions of n in which all nonzero multiplicities are distinct, and let sigma_n be the involution on T(n) obtained by interchanging the list of parts with the list of multiplicities and then reordering so that the multiplicities are increasing. Determine the asymptotic number of fixed points of sigma_n.
accepted.context_brief: Fixed points of the parts-multiplicities involution

evidence.quote: Wilf (2010) mentions a mapping on T(n) in which the roles of parts and multiplicities are interchanged. We let sigma_n denote this mapping.
It is an open problem to find (asymptotics for) the number of fixed points of sigma_n.
